G4524.forms: Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος)

G4523.strongs: a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite

G4572.root: genitive case from [[w:G4571]] and [[w:G0846]], also dative case of the same, σεαυτῷ, and accusative case σεαυτόν, likewise contracted σαυτοῦ, σαυτῷ, and σαυτόν, respectively
senses: (in NT not contracted, σαυτοῦ, as in Att..), reflex. prop. of 2nd of person(s) sing., used only in genitive, dative and accusative (of, to) thyself: [[r:MAT.4.6|Mat 4:6]], [[r:JHN.8.13|Jhn 8:13]], [[r:1TI.4.16|1Ti 4:16]], al. (In Hellenistic, the pl. is ἑαυτῶν (which see), not ὑμῶν αὐτῶν as in Attic, see Bl., § 13, 1.) † (AS)

G4567.root: of Chaldee origin corresponding to [[w:H4566]] (with the definite affix)

G4583.root: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of [[w:G4582]]
senses: σεληνιάζω (σελήνη), act, in Manetho (Caren., 4, 81), in NT depon. -ομαι, to be moonstruck, i.e. epileptic (epilepsy being supposed to be influenced by the moon): [[r:MAT.4.24|Mat 4:24 17:15]].† (AS)

G4537.strongs: to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively)
senses: σαλπίζω to sound a trumpet: [[r:REV.8.6|Rev 8:6]] ff. [[r:REV.9.1|Rev 9:1, 13 10:7 11:15]]; metaphorically, [[r:MAT.6.2|Mat 6:2.]] Impers., the trumpet sounds: [[r:1CO.15.52|1Co 15:52.]]† (AS)

G4505.root: prolongation from [[w:G4506]] in its original sense
senses: in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers.

In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, [[r:MAT.6.2|Mat 6:2]], [[r:LUK.14.21|Luk 14:21]] [[r:ACT.9.11|Act 9:11 12:10]] (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).† (AS)

G4594.root: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article [[w:G3588]] (t changed to s) and [[w:G2250]]
G4594.strongs: on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto)
senses: adv., to-day: [[r:MAT.6.11|Mat 6:11]], [[r:LUK.4.21|Luk 4:21]], [[r:ACT.4.9|Act 4:9]], al.; opposite to αὔριον, [[r:MAT.6.30|Mat 6:30]], [[r:LUK.12.28|Luk 12:28]], [[r:JAS.4.13|Jas 4:13]]; χθὲς καὶ σ. καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας, [[r:HEB.13.8|Heb 13:8]]; ἡ σ. ἡμέρα, [[r:ACT.20.20|Act 20:20]]; ἕως (ἄχρι) τῆς σ. ἡμέρας, [[r:ROM.11.8|Rom 11:8]], [[r:2CO.3.14|2Co 3:14]]; μέχρι (ἕως) τῆς σ. (sc. ἡμέρας), [[r:MAT.11.23|Mat 11:23 27:8]]; as subst., τὸ σ., [[r:HEB.3.13|Heb 3:13]]; id. in appos., ὁρίζει ἡμὶραν, σ., [[r:HEB.4.7|Heb 4:7]] R, mg., (see Westc., in l) (AS)

G4506.root: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to [[w:G4482]] (through the idea of a current
G4506.strongs: compare); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue
senses: ῥύομαι to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), [[r:MAT.27.43|Mat 27:43]], [[r:2PE.2.7|2Pe 2:7]]; id. before ἀπό, [[r:MAT.6.13|Mat 6:13]], [[r:LUK.11.4|Luk 11:4]] (Rec., R, mg.), [[r:2TI.4.18|2Ti 4:18]]; before ἐκ, [[r:ROM.7.24|Rom 7:24]], [[r:2CO.1.10|2Co 1:10]], [[r:COL.1.13|Col 1:13]], [[r:1TH.1.10|1Th 1:10]], [[r:2TI.3.11|2Ti 3:11]], [[r:2PE.2.9|2Pe 2:9]]; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, [[r:ROM.11.26|Rom 11:26.]] Passive: before ἀπό, [[r:ROM.15.31|Rom 15:31]], [[r:2TH.3.2|2Th 3:2]]; before ἐκ, [[r:LUK.1.74|Luk 1:74]], [[r:2TI.4.17|2Ti 4:17]].† (AS)
σής σητός (late genitive for cl. σεός), ὁ, a moth, clothes moth: [[r:MAT.6.19|Mat 6:19-20]], [[r:LUK.12.33|Luk 12:33]].† (AS)

rotten, corrupt, bad, worth­less: of trees and fruit (opposite to ἀγαθός, καλός), [[r:MAT.7.17|Mat 7:17-18 12:33]] [[r:LUK.6.43|Luk 6:43]]; of fish, [[r:MAT.13.48|Mat 13:48.]] Metaphorical, in moral sense: λόγος σ., [[r:EPH.4.29|Eph 4:29.]] "In Hellenistic... it became a synonym for αἰσχρός or κακός," MM, xxii.† (AS)

G4578.strongs: a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake
senses: (σείω), a shaking, commotion, as a tempest at sea: [[r:MAT.8.24|Mat 8:24]]; esp. an earthquake: [[r:MAT.24.7|Mat 24:7 27:54 28:2]], [[r:MRK.13.8|Mrk 13:8]], [[r:LUK.21.11|Luk 21:11]], [[r:ACT.16.26|Act 16:26]], [[r:REV.6.12|Rev 6:12 8:5 11:13, 19 16:18]].† (AS)

G4541.strongs: a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria
senses: (-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό, a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): [[r:MAT.10.5|Mat 10:5]], [[r:LUK.9.52|Luk 9:52 10:33 17:16]], [[r:JHN.4.9|Jhn 4:9, 39-40]], [[r:ACT.8.25|Act 8:25]]; as an opprobrious epithet, [[r:JHN.8.48|Jhn 8:48.]]† (AS)

G4531.strongs: to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite
G4531.kjv: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up
senses: (σάλος), prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, [[r:MAT.11.7|Mat 11:7]], [[r:LUK.7.24|Luk 7:24]]; a house, [[r:LUK.6.48|Luk 6:48]], [[r:ACT.4.31|Act 4:31 16:26]]; the earth, [[r:HEB.12.26|Heb 12:26]]; the heavenly bodies, [[r:MAT.24.29|Mat 24:29]], [[r:MRK.13.25|Mrk 13:25]], [[r:LUK.21.26|Luk 21:26]]; of a vessel shaken in filling, [[r:LUK.6.38|Luk 6:38.]] Metaphorical,
to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., [[r:HEB.12.27|Heb 12:27]];
with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: [[r:ACT.2.25|Act 2:25]] (LXX); (with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, [[r:2TH.2.2|2Th 2:2]];

G4526.strongs: "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief)
senses: σάκκος also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ (cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX),
a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: [[r:REV.6.12|Rev 6:12.]]
a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: [[r:MAT.11.21|Mat 11:21]], [[r:LUK.10.13|Luk 10:13]], [[r:REV.11.3|Rev 11:3]].† (AS)

G4521.forms: σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά
G4521.strongs: the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications
senses: the seventh day of the week, the sabbath

the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: [[r:MAT.12.8|Mat 12:8]], [[r:MRK.2.27|Mrk 2:27]], [[r:LUK.6.5|Luk 6:5]], al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, [[r:EXO.20.8|Exo 20:8]], al., usually τῶν σ., see infr.), [[r:LUK.13.16|Luk 13:16 14:5]]; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, [[r:ACT.1.12|Act 1:12]] (cf. [[r:MAT.24.29|Mat 24:29]]); dative, of time (τῷ) σ., [[r:LUK.6.9|Luk 6:9 14:1]]; ἐν (τῷ) σ., [[r:MAT.12.2|Mat 12:2]], [[r:LUK.6.7|Luk 6:7]], [[r:JHN.5.16|Jhn 5:16]], al.; accusative, of duration, τὸ σ., [[r:LUK.23.56|Luk 23:56]]; κατὰ πᾶν σ., [[r:ACT.13.27|Act 13:27 15:21 18:4]]; pl., σ. τρία, [[r:ACT.17.2|Act 17:2]] R, txt. (but see infr.);

as most frequently in LXX (see Swete, Mk., 17; Thackeray, Gr., 35) the pl. form, τὰ σ. (see supr. on the Aram. form. There is also an analogy in the names of other festivals, τ. ἐγκαίνια, ἄζυμα, etc.): [[r:MAT.28.1|Mat 28:1]], [[r:COL.2.16|Col 2:16]]; ἡ ἡμέρα τῶν σ. ([[r:EXO.20.8|Exo 20:8]], al.), [[r:LUK.4.16|Luk 4:16]], [[r:ACT.13.14|Act 13:14 16:13]]; dative pl. (in LXX -τοις, but [[r:1MA.2.38|1Ma 2:38]] as in NT) by metaplasmus (El., § 9, 3), σάββασι, [[r:MAT.12.1|Mat 12:1, 5 12:10-12]] [[r:MRK.1.21|Mrk 1:21 2:23 3:2, 4]], [[r:LUK.4.31|Luk 4:31 6:2]].

the sing. form: πρώτη σαββάτσυ, [[r:MRK.16.9|Mrk 16:9]]; δὶς τοῦ σ. (Bl., § 35, 4; 36, 13), [[r:LUK.18.12|Luk 18:12]]; κατὰ μίαν σαββάτου, [[r:1CO.16.2|1Co 16:2]]; pl., σ. τρία, [[r:ACT.17.2|Act 17:2]] R, mg. (but see supr.);

the pl. form: ἡ μία τῶν σ. (where the genitive = μετὰ τά; Soph., Lex., 43a), [[r:MAT.28.1|Mat 28:1]], [[r:MRK.16.2|Mrk 16:2]], [[r:LUK.24.1|Luk 24:1]], [[r:JHN.20.1|Jhn 20:1, 19]], [[r:ACT.20.7|Act 20:7]] (AS)

G4570.root: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb
senses: σβέννυμι of fire or things on fire, to quench: with accusative, [[r:MAT.12.20|Mat 12:20]], [[r:EPH.6.16|Eph 6:16]], [[r:HEB.11.34|Heb 11:34]]; pass., [[r:MAT.25.8|Mat 25:8]], [[r:MRK.9.48|Mrk 9:48]],. Metaphorical (cf. [[r:SNG.8.7|Sng 8:7]], 4Ma.16:4): τὸ πνεῦμα, [[r:1TH.5.19|1Th 5:19.]]† ζβέννυμι, for σβ-, [[r:1TH.5.19|1Th 5:19]] T (see WH, Notes, 148).† (AS)

G4592.root: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of [[w:G4591]]
G4592.strongs: an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally
senses: of that which distinguishes a person or thing from others: [[r:MAT.26.48|Mat 26:48]] [[r:LUK.2.12|Luk 2:12]], [[r:2TH.3.17|2Th 3:17]] (cf. Deiss., LAE, 153.2); before genitive epexeg., [[r:ROM.4.11|Rom 4:11]]; with genitive obj., [[r:MAT.24.8|Mat 24:8, 30]], [[r:2CO.12.12|2Co 12:12]]; with genitive subj., [[r:MAT.16.3|Mat 16:3]];

a sign of warning or admonition: [[r:MAT.12.39|Mat 12:39 16:4]], [[r:LUK.2.34|Luk 2:34 11:29-30]], [[r:1CO.14.22|1Co 14:22]]; (with) a sign portending future events (Soph., Plat. al.): [[r:MRK.13.4|Mrk 13:4]], [[r:LUK.21.7|Luk 21:7, 11 21:25]], [[r:ACT.2.19|Act 2:19]], [[r:REV.12.1|Rev 12:1, 3 15:1]];

G4563.root: from a derivative of σαίρω (to brush off
G4563.strongs: akin to); meaning a broom; to sweep
senses: late form of σαίρω, to sweep: with accusative, [[r:LUK.15.8|Luk 15:8]]; pass., [[r:MAT.12.44|Mat 12:44]], [[r:LUK.11.25|Luk 11:25]].† (AS)

G4568.strongs: a certain measure for things dry
senses: (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): [[r:MAT.13.33|Mat 13:33]], [[r:LUK.13.21|Luk 13:21]].† (AS)

G4522.root: from a derivative of σάττω (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope)

G4576.root: middle voice of an apparently primary verb
senses: σέβω to worship: with accusative of person(s), [[r:MAT.15.9|Mat 15:9]], [[r:MRK.7.7|Mrk 7:7]], [[r:ACT.18.13|Act 18:13 19:27]]; σεβόμενος τ. θεόν, [[r:ACT.16.14|Act 16:14 18:7]]; σεβόμενοι (σ. προσήλυτοι, σ. Ἕλληνες), devout, [[r:ACT.13.43|Act 13:43, 50 17:4, 17]] (cf. προσήλυτος).† (AS)

G4561.strongs: flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such)
senses: prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: [[r:1CO.15.39|1Co 15:39]], [[r:2CO.12.7|2Co 12:7]], [[r:GAL.6.13|Gal 6:13]], al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, [[r:1CO.5.50|1Co 5:50]]; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, [[r:LUK.24.39|Luk 24:39]]; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), [[r:REV.17.16|Rev 17:16 19:18]]; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. with (cf. κατεσθίειν, [[r:2KI.9.36|4Ki.9:36]], al., and βιβρώσκειν, frequently in l.); metaphorically, [[r:JAS.5.3|Jas 5:3]]; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, [[r:JHN.6.52|Jhn 6:52-56]];

Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: [[r:ACT.2.26|Act 2:26]] (LXX), 31, [[r:2CO.12.7|2Co 12:7]], [[r:GAL.4.14|Gal 4:14]], [[r:EPH.5.29|Eph 5:29]]; μία σ., [[r:MRK.10.8|Mrk 10:8]]; εἰς σ. μίαν ([[r:GEN.2.24|Gen 2:24]]), [[r:MAT.19.5|Mat 19:5]], [[r:MRK.10.8|Mrk 10:8]], [[r:1CO.6.16|1Co 6:16]], [[r:EPH.5.31|Eph 5:31]]; hence, of the material as opposite to the immaterial part of man (cf. Lft., Notes, 88): opposite to πνεῦμα, [[r:1CO.5.5|1Co 5:5]], [[r:2CO.7.1|2Co 7:1]], [[r:COL.2.5|Col 2:5]], [[r:1PE.3.18|1Pe 3:18, 4:6]]; to ψύχη, [[r:ACT.2.31|Act 2:31]], Rec.; of the present life, ἐν (τῇ) σ., [[r:ROM.7.5|Rom 7:5]], [[r:GAL.2.20|Gal 2:20]], [[r:PHP.1.22|Php 1:22, 24]] [[r:1PE.4.2|1Pe 4:2]]; of Christ's life on earth, αἱ ἡμέραι τ. σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ, [[r:HEB.5.7|Heb 5:7]]; of things pertaining to the body, ἐν (τῇ) σ., [[r:GAL.6.12|Gal 6:12, 13]] [[r:PHP.3.3|Php 3:3]], 4.

of natural origin and relationship ([[r:GEN.2.24|Gen 2:24]], [[r:ISA.58.7|Isa 58:7]], al.): τέκνα τῆς σ., [[r:ROM.9.8|Rom 9:8]]; κατὰ σάρκα, ib. 3, 5, [[r:1CO.10.18|1Co 10:18]], [[r:GAL.4.23|Gal 4:23, 29]]; ἡ σ. μου, [[r:ROM.11.14|Rom 11:14]] (cf. [[r:JDG.9.2|Jdg 9:2]], [[r:2SA.5.1|2Ki 5:1]], al.).
Of the physical nature as subject to sensation and desire (Plut.),

without any ethical disparagement: [[r:ROM.7.18|Rom 7:18 13:14]]; opposite to πνεῦμα, [[r:MAT.26.41|Mat 26:41]], [[r:MRK.14.38|Mrk 14:38]]; τ. θέλημα τῆς σ., [[r:JHN.1.13|Jhn 1:13]]; ἡ ἐπιθυμία τῆς σ., [[r:1JN.2.16|1Jn 2:16]]; pl., [[r:2PE.2.18|2Pe 2:18]]; παθεῖν σαρκί, [[r:1PE.4.1|1Pe 4:1]];

in ethical sense, esp. in Pauline Epp., of the flesh as the seat and vehicle of sinful desires: opposite to νοῦς, [[r:ROM.7.25|Rom 7:25]]; to πνεῦμα, [[r:ROM.8.4|Rom 8:4-9, 12, 13]], [[r:GAL.5.16|Gal 5:16, 17 19 6:8]] (cf. DB, ii, 14f.; iv, 165f.; Cremer, 844ff.). (AS)

G4579.strongs: to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern)
senses: σείω to shake, move to and fro: τ. γῆν, [[r:HEB.12.26|Heb 12:26]] (LXX); pass., ἡ γῆ, [[r:MAT.27.51|Mat 27:51]] (LXX); συκῆ, [[r:REV.6.13|Rev 6:13.]] Metaphorical, to agitate, stir up, with fear or some other emotion: [[r:MAT.21.10|Mat 21:10 28:4]] (cf. ἀνα-, δια-, κατα-σείω).† (AS)

G4582.strongs: probably akin to the alternate of, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon

G4536.root: perhaps from [[w:G4535]] (through the idea of quavering or reverberation)
senses: a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: [[r:1CO.14.8|1Co 14:8]], [[r:HEB.12.19|Heb 12:19]], [[r:REV.1.10|Rev 1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14]] By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, [[r:MAT.24.31|Mat 24:31]]; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, [[r:1TH.4.16|1Th 4:16]]; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., [[r:1CO.15.52|1Co 15:52.]]† (AS)

G4518.root: of Chaldee or ([[w:H7662]] with pronominal suffix)
G4518.strongs: thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress
senses: σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי), sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: [[r:MAT.27.46|Mat 27:46]], [[r:MRK.15.34|Mrk 15:34]] ([[r:PSA.22.2|Psa 22:2]], Heb. עָזַב).† ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב), zaphthanei: [[r:MAT.27.46|Mat 27:46]] (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).† (AS)

G4511.root: from [[w:G4506]] in the sense of its congener [[w:G4482]]

G4547.root: neuter of a derivative of σάνδαλον (a "sandal"
G4547.strongs: of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad

G4501.strongs: a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively)
senses: a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: [[r:REV.1.16|Rev 1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21]]; metaphorically, [[r:LUK.2.35|Luk 2:35.]]† (AS)

G4558.strongs: Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine

G4540.strongs: Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine

senses: in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: [[r:LUK.21.25|Luk 21:25.]]† (AS)

G4542.strongs: a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria
senses: in FlJ (B.J., i, 21, 2, al.), the region of Samaria.

(σῆμα, a sign), to give a sign, signify, indicate: with accusative of thing(s), [[r:ACT.25.27|Act 25:27]], [[r:REV.1.1|Rev 1:1]] (cf. MM, xxii); with accusative and inf., [[r:ACT.11.28|Act 11:28]]; before quæst. indir., [[r:JHN.12.33|Jhn 12:33 18:32 21:19]].† (AS)

G4515.root: adverb from a presumed derivative of [[w:G4516]]
G4515.strongs: Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language

G4569.forms: Σαῦλος, -ου, ὁ (Hellenized form of Σαούλ, which see)
G4569.root: of Hebrew origin, the same as [[w:G4549]]
G4569.strongs: Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul

G4549.strongs: Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul
senses: the Jewish name of the Apostle Paul, used in the indecl. form only in address (cf. Σαῦλος): [[r:ACT.9.4|Act 9:4, 17 22:7, 13 26:14]].† (AS)

G4565.strongs: Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine

G4529.root: probably from [[w:G4535]] (from the surge on the shore)

G4517.strongs: probably akin to); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye)
senses: to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): [[r:ACT.15.29|Act 15:29 23:30]] Rec., R, mg.† (AS)

G4543.strongs: Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean
senses: (-θράκη, BE), -ης, ἡ Samothrace, an island in the Ægean: [[r:ACT.16.11|Act 16:11.]]† (AS)

G4574.strongs: something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc)

G4516.strongs: strength; Roma, the capital of Italy

G4544.strongs: Samus, an island of the Mediterranean

G4575.strongs: venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial
senses: In late writers, with reference to the Roman Imperial name;
ὁ Σ., Augustus, i.e. the Roman Emperor: [[r:ACT.25.21|Act 25:21, 25]];

G4573.root: middle voice from a derivative of [[w:G4576]]

G4564.strongs: Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham

G4560.strongs: similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft

(Rec. has -ικός in all these passages except [[r:2CO.3.3|2Co 3:3]], but the evidence is decisive against it.)† SYN.: σαρκικός, q.v (AS)
